groups.title: LHC performance
groups.caption: L-GATr achieves state-of-the-art performance across amplitude regression, jet classification, and event generation at the LHC.

groups.title: LHC ML context
groups.caption: Modern ML is transforming LHC science, but standard architectures struggle with precision requirements, large datasets, and simulation–measurement gaps.

groups.title: equivariance interpretation
groups.caption: Interpreting the benefits of Lorentz equivariance for jet tagging, activation design, and the combined role of equivariance with pre-training.

groups.title: L-GATr overview
groups.caption: L-GATr extends GATr to Lorentz equivariance and is applied to amplitude regression, jet tagging, and event generation in this physics-targeted study.

groups.title: physics task context
groups.caption: Background on LHC amplitude regression and jet tagging tasks, their precision requirements, and how equivariance addresses scaling challenges.

groups.title: algebra definitions
groups.caption: Formal definitions of the spacetime geometric algebra, its product rules, layer operations (linear, attention, LayerNorm, activation), and the CFM diffusion framework.

groups.title: algebra interpretations
groups.caption: Interpretations of spacetime algebra objects: bivectors as planes, grade structure, Lorentz transformation properties, and physical meaning of algebra grades.

groups.title: multivector representation
groups.caption: Methods for representing spacetime objects and Lorentz transformations as multivectors, and measuring the scaling behavior of L-GATr on GPU.

groups.title: equivariant architecture
groups.caption: L-GATr encodes exact Lorentz equivariance via grade-respecting linear layers, multivector attention, layer normalization, and geometric product nonlinearity.

groups.title: symmetry breaking benefits
groups.caption: Enforcing equivariance and selectively breaking it with reference vectors outperforms fully symmetry-broken networks across all LHC applications.

groups.title: reference multivectors
groups.caption: Reference multivectors enable tunable partial symmetry breaking by encoding the beam direction and detector geometry as additional network inputs.

groups.title: efficiency interpretation
groups.caption: Transformer and GNN resource efficiency differs primarily in memory and compute scaling; L-GATr's FlashAttention use drives its favorable efficiency over CGENN.

groups.title: benchmark results
groups.caption: L-GATr matches or outperforms all baselines on top tagging, JetClass, and pre-trained fine-tuning benchmarks, including parameter-efficiency comparisons.

groups.title: amplitude regression
groups.caption: L-GATr guarantees exact Lorentz invariance and leads in amplitude regression for high-multiplicity final states, outperforming DSI and MLPs.

groups.title: amplitude setup
groups.caption: Amplitude regression training uses MadGraph data with standardized log-amplitudes; baselines include MLP, transformer, GAP, DSI, and CGENN.

groups.title: top tagging setup
groups.caption: Top tagging uses 2M jets from Pythia+Delphes with ATLAS card; baselines include LorentzNet, PELICAN, CGENN, ParT, and MIParT.

claims.sentence: "L-GATr yields state-of-the-art performance for a wide range of machine learning tasks at the Large Hadron Collider."
"L-GATr represents data in a geometric algebra over space-time and is equivariant under Lorentz transformations."
"The underlying architecture is a versatile and scalable transformer, which is able to break symmetries if needed."
"For amplitude regression, jet classification, and event generation, we find significant improvements over previous architectures."

"Modern machine learning is poised to define much of the future program at the Large Hadron Collider, from triggering and data acquisition to object identification, anomaly searches, non-perturbative input, theory and detector simulations, and simulation-based inference."

"The question is no longer if deep neural networks will be used for all of these purposes; it is how we can ensure that these networks provide optimal and resilient results, including a comprehensive uncertainty treatment."
"Standard architectures do not capture amplitudes or densities at the per-mille level."
"The target precision for LHC applications requires huge datasets even by cheap simulation standards."
"Small deviations between simulated and measured data require networks to be tuned on measurements."
"Learning the Minkowski metric is a known challenge for all networks working on relativistic phase space."
"One could work with Lorentz-invariant or Lorentz-covariant internal representations and save the networks the time and effort to learn such a representation for each task."

"The first modern ML applications in LHC physics were jet taggers, which aimed to optimally analyze the substructure of jets to identify their partonic nature based on all available low-level information."
"Jet taggers triggered the question of how and whether to include Lorentz symmetry, leading to a set of Lorentz-equivariant jet taggers, currently under experimental study."
"L-GATr is based on the Geometric Algebra Transformer (GATr), designed for Euclidean translations, rotations, and reflections."
"L-GATr generalizes GATr by encoding exact Lorentz-equivariance into new network layers, including a maximally expressive linear map, attention, and layer normalization."
"The architecture was originally developed for an ML audience and applied to amplitude regression, top tagging, and event generation in Ref. [35]."

"In this physics-targeted study, we extend the amplitude regression analysis, improve the classification through pre-training and multi-class tagging, and deliver a competitive generative network for Monte Carlo event generation."
"A geometric algebra is defined as an extension of a vector space with an extra composition law — the geometric product."

"The geometric product of two vectors x and y is decomposed into a symmetric and an antisymmetric contribution, x y = {x, y}/2 + [x, y]/2, where the anti-commutator {x, y}/2 represents the usual inner product, and [x, y]/2 constitutes a new outer product."
"The spacetime algebra G1,3 is built from the vector space R4 with the metric g = diag(1,−1,−1,−1), with a basis of four real vectors γµ satisfying the anti-commutation relation {γµ,γν} = 2gµν."
"The relation {γµ,γν} = 2gµν is the defining property of the gamma matrices, the basis elements of the Dirac algebra used to describe spinor interactions."
"The antisymmetric tensor σµν is generated from the geometric product of two γµ and has grade two: γµγν = gµν + σµν."
"σµν is a bivector, which can be interpreted as the plane defined by µ and ν in Minkowski space."
"The pseudoscalar γ5 = γ0γ1γ2γ3 ≡ (1/4!)εµνρσγµγνγργσ can be obtained through the product of all four γµ."
"Pseudoscalars act as parity reversal operations on any object and can be used to write axial vectors as γµγ5."
"The missing factor i compared to the usual definition of γ5 indicates the slight difference between the complex Dirac algebra and the real spacetime algebra."
"Any multivector of the algebra can be expressed as x = xS 1 + x V µ γµ + x B µν σµν + xA µ γµγ5 + x P γ5, where each component is in R16."
"Multivectors can be used to represent both spacetime objects and Lorentz transformations."
"Particles can be characterized by their type (particle identification, or PID) and their 4-momentum pµ, with xS = PID, x V µ = pµ, and other components set to zero."
"The spacetime algebra naturally structures relevant objects like parity-violating transition amplitudes."
"The matrix element M can be decomposed into parity-even and parity-odd terms as |M|2 = |ME|2 + |MO|2 + 2Re(M*E MO)."

"Lorentz transformations can be applied on spacetime objects as Λv(x) = vxv−1, where v is a multivector representing an element of the Lorentz group acting on the algebra element x, and v−1 is its corresponding inverse."
"A multivector encoding an object that is invariant under a Lorentz transformation will also represent the transformation itself."
"Boosts along the z-axis are generated by σ03, and the multivector for a boost with rapidity ω is v = eωσ03/2 = cosh(ω/2) + σ03 sinh(ω/2)."
"Lorentz transformations will never mix grades; each algebra grade transforms under a separate sub-representation of the Lorentz group."
"The spacetime algebra G1,3 covers only a limited range of Lorentz tensor representations and cannot represent symmetric rank-2 tensors."
"For most LHC applications, one does not encounter higher-order tensor representations as inputs or outputs, so this is not a substantial limitation."
"L-GATr is exactly equivariant under Lorentz group transformations Λ: L-GATr(Λ(x)) = Λ(L-GATr(x))."
"Multivector grades form sub-representations of the Lorentz group, with all multivector components of the same grade transforming equally under all network operations."
"The L-GATr architecture uses variations of the standard transformer operations Linear, Attention, LayerNorm, and Activation, adapted to process multivectors."

"The most general linear combination of independently-transforming multivector components is Linear(x) = Σ(k=0 to 4) vk⟨x⟩k + Σ(k=0 to 4) wkγ5⟨x⟩k, where v, w ∈ R5 are learnable parameters and k runs over the five algebra grades."
"The second term in the linear layer is optional and breaks the symmetry down to the special orthochronous Lorentz group."
"The scaled dot-product attention for multivectors is Attention(q, k, v)ic = Σ(j=1 to nt) Softmaxj(Σ(c'=1 to nc) ⟨qic', kjc'⟩ / sqrt(16nc)) vjc, where ⟨·,·⟩ is the G1,3 inner product."
"The G1,3 inner product can be pre-computed as a list of signs and a Euclidean inner product, allowing the use of standard transformer implementations."
"Layer normalization on multivectors is defined as LayerNorm(x) = x / sqrt((1/nc) Σ(c=1 to nc) Σ(k=0 to 4) |⟨xc⟩k, ⟨xc⟩k⟩| + ε), where ε = 10^−2 is a normalization constant."
"Layer normalization is non-trivial on multivectors because the G1,3 norm can have zero and negative contributions."
"The specific value of ε in layer normalization has a negligible impact on the performance of the network."
"Activation functions applied directly on the multivectors break the equivariance."
"Scalar-gated activation functions are employed, where the whole multivector is scaled by a nonlinearity acting only on the scalar component: Activation(x) = GELU(⟨x⟩0) x."
"The geometric algebra allows the geometric product as a source of nonlinearity: GP(x, y) = x y, which is equivariant itself with the property GP(vxv−1, v yv−1) = vGP(x, y)v−1."

"The full L-GATr architecture is built as: x̄ = LayerNorm(x), AttentionBlock(x) = Linear ◦ Attention(Linear(x̄), Linear(x̄), Linear(x̄)) + x, MLPBlock(x) = Linear ◦ Activation ◦ Linear ◦ GP(Linear(x̄), Linear(x̄)) + x, Block(x) = MLPBlock ◦ AttentionBlock(x), and L-GATr(x) = Linear ◦ Block ◦ Block ◦ ... ◦ Block ◦ Linear(x)."

"Multivector channels can be supplemented with extra scalar channels to allow a smooth transition to standard transformers and to feed large amounts of scalar information without overloading the multivector channels."
"In many LHC contexts, Lorentz symmetry is only partially preserved."
"If partial symmetry breaking is not accounted for when applying a Lorentz-equivariant architecture, performance can degrade significantly."

"Lorentz-equivariant architectures inherently treat inputs related by global Lorentz transformations as equivalent, and in the presence of symmetry breaking, these inputs may carry different physical information."
"A fully Lorentz-equivariant architecture is, by construction, blind to differences when symmetry is broken, which can limit its effectiveness."
"L-GATr can apply partial symmetry breaking in a tunable manner by including reference multivectors as additional inputs."
"Any network operation that involves a reference vector will violate equivariance, breaking the symmetry group to a subgroup where the reference direction is fixed."
"The network has the option to tune out the reference vectors in certain phase space regions or even globally if they are not required."
"Enforcing symmetry in the network and then allowing the network to break it with reference vectors produces better results than a network where the symmetry is completely broken."
"Reference multivectors are appended for each L-GATr input x in the same way, either as extra tokens, or as extra channels within each token."

"When applying data augmentation, one should augment only the input particle data, and then append the reference multivectors directly before processing the particles with the Lorentz-equivariant architecture."
"The LHC beam direction breaks the Lorentz group to the subgroup of rotations around and boosts along the beam axis."
"The natural reference vector for beam direction is the beam direction itself, which can be implemented as two vectors x V ± = (0,0,0,±1), or one bivector representing the x−y plane, x B 12 = 1."
"Similar performance is achieved for both choices of beam direction representation."
"The detector setup can compromise the symmetry of the observables with respect to relativistic boosts."
"The Lorentz group can be broken to the subgroup of rotations in three-dimensional space SO(3) using the reference multivector x V = (1,0,0,0)."
"Reference multivectors x V ± = (1,0,0,±1), representing the beam with a non-zero time component, break full Lorentz equivariance down to SO(3) equivariance under spatial rotations."
"Reference multivectors are included as extra tokens for jet tagging in Section 4, and as extra channels for generation in Section 5."
"Symmetry breaking is crucial for both jet tagging and event generation, and the specific way it is implemented has a strong impact on the network performance."
"Additional kinematic inputs like pT, E, ∆R are embedded as scalars for jet tagging, which are only invariant under the subgroup of rotations around the beam axis."
"For event generation, the m and pT CFM-velocity components are extracted from scalar output channels of L-GATr and used to overwrite the equivariantly predicted velocity components."
"Fully connected graph neural networks and transformers both process data as sets of tokens and both respect full or partial permutation symmetry."
"Resource efficiency is where graph neural networks and transformers differ most."
"Scaling of speed and memory consumption is measured on an H100 GPU by evaluating the network on datasets containing a single event and a varying number of particles."
"For transformer-based architectures in the scaling test, the attention receives inputs with 72 channels from 4 attention heads."
"For L-GATr, the scaling test architecture is built with 8 multivector channels and 16 scalar channels to achieve 72 total attention input channels."
"L-GATr consists of 2.3 × 10^4 parameters, the transformer consists of 6.7 × 10^5 parameters, and CGENN consists of 2.5 × 10^4 parameters."
"The evaluation time of all networks is independent of the number of tokens in the few-token regime, but it eventually scales quadratically."
"The transition from constant to quadratic scaling happens when attention or message passing, rather than other parallelizable operations, becomes the limiting factor."
"L-GATr scales like a standard transformer in the many-token regime because they both use the same attention module."
"For few tokens, L-GATr is slower than a standard transformer because of more expensive linear layers."
"CGENN is slower than L-GATr for few tokens, and the quadratic scaling due to the expensive message passing operation takes off sooner."
"For many particles, L-GATr and the standard transformer display the same linear scaling in memory usage with the number of tokens since they use the same attention module."
"CGENN scales quadratically in memory in the many-particle regime and runs out of memory already for 1000 particles."
"The difference in memory scaling between L-GATr and CGENN is attributable to the different degree of optimization in the architectures."
"L-GATr uses FlashAttention, heavily optimized for speed and memory efficiency."
"Graph neural networks are often optimized for sparsely connected graphs, so the efficiency of the standard implementation degrades for fully connected graphs."
"Partonic scattering amplitudes can be calculated exactly as a function of phase space."
"The evaluation of scattering amplitudes can become very expensive if high-order corrections and a large number of external particles are included."
"Amplitude surrogates as part of standard event generators speed up precision predictions."
"Standard neural networks struggle to reach sufficient accuracy for amplitudes with a high amount of external particles."
"L-GATr uses the partial permutation symmetry of particles in the processes to efficiently scale to high multiplicities."
"L-GATr guarantees the exact Lorentz invariance of the amplitude."
"Training data for amplitude regression consists of 4 × 10^5 training data points for each multiplicity up to 4 gluons generated with MadGraph at LO in QCD."
"To avoid divergences in amplitude regression, globally pT > 20 GeV and ∆R > 0.4 for all final-state objects are required."
"L-GATr is trained on standardized logarithmic amplitudes A = (log A − log Ā) / σ_log A."
"Benchmarks for amplitude regression include a standard MLP, a standard transformer, the Geometric Algebra Perceptron (GAP), a deep sets network (DSI), and CGENN."
"All amplitude regression networks are trained with 4-momenta inputs except DSI, which also takes pairwise Minkowski products of 4-momenta as inputs."
"For Z + ng amplitudes with increasing particle multiplicity, transformer and graph networks scale better than MLPs."
"L-GATr is roughly on par with the leading DSI network for a small number of gluons, but its improved scaling gives it the lead for higher-multiplicity final states."

"The scaling improvement of L-GATr is consistent with the equivariant approximation theorem, which establishes that the number of parameters needed to approximate an equivariant function to a given accuracy decreases proportionally to the dimension of the symmetry group acting on the input space."
"L-GATr performs well when trained on all processes jointly using a single network."
"L-GATr stands as a top performer on all training regimes when scaling with the size of the training dataset."
"For small training sets, L-GATr and CGENN are very efficient thanks to their equivariant operations."
"For Z + 5 gluon productions, 4 × 10^4 points are generated, and the L-GATr size is reduced to 4 × 10^4 parameters and the baselines to 10^4 parameters to prevent overfitting."
"For the Z + 5 gluons case, datasets are reduced to 4 × 10^4 points to keep the comparison fair."
"L-GATr reproduces its scaling behavior for Z + 5 gluons despite the more complex process and less generous training."
"For optimization challenges caused by the small data regime, L-GATr is compared to the transformer and DSI, representing an attention-based network and a symmetry-enforcing network respectively."
"Jet tagging is arguably the LHC task which is currently impacted most by modern ML."
"Two approaches stand out as top performers in jet tagging: transformer-based architectures and equivariant networks."
"L-GATr sets a new record for jet tagging by combining the merits of equivariance and transformer-based architectures."
"The top tagging dataset consists of 2 M top quark and QCD jets with pT,j = 550...650 GeV."
"The top tagging dataset was generated with Pythia 8 and interfaced with Delphes for detector simulation using the default ATLAS card."
"L-GATr is trained and evaluated on the top tagging dataset following the standard train/validation/test splitting of 1.2/0.4/0.4 M."
"Baselines for jet tagging comparison include LorentzNet, PELICAN, CGENN, ParT, and MIParT."
"On the top tagging challenge, L-GATr is at least on par with the leading equivariant baselines."
"For all tagging tests, reference vectors include the beam direction as the x−y plane bivector, x B 12 = 1, and the time reference x V = (1,0,0,0)."
"Including both the beam direction and the time reference significantly contributes to boosting the tagging performance."
"The best performing setup according to the area under the curve (AUC) is used for all tagging experiments."
"The background rejection is considered for the tagging setup choice, but is not used as a deciding factor due to its larger uncertainty."

"The JetClass dataset covers a wide variety of jet signatures with signal events consisting of jets from multiple decay modes of top quarks, W, Z and Higgs bosons, and background events from light quark and gluon jets."
"JetClass events are generated with MadGraph and Pythia, with detector effects simulated with Delphes using the default CMS card."
"A kinematic cut pT,j = 500...1000 GeV and |ηj| < 2.0 is applied to all jets in the JetClass dataset."
"JetClass contains 100 M jets equally distributed across 10 classes."

"JetClass provides input features of four main categories: the 4-momenta of the jet particles, kinematic variables like ∆R and log pT, particle identification variables, and trajectory displacement variables."
"When passing JetClass features through L-GATr, all features besides the 4-momenta are embedded to the network as scalar channels."
"The same architecture as top tagging is used for all JetClass tests."
"The L-GATr tagger achieves a significant improvement over the previous state-of-the-art, ParT and MIParT, in essentially all signal types on JetClass."
"The quality of L-GATr predictions steadily increases as more features are added to the training data."
"L-GATr achieves a performance similar to the non-equivariant ParT and MIParT taggers even if trained with only 10% of all available jets."
"The large capacity of transformer architectures motivates using pre-training to further improve the tagging performance."
"L-GATr is pre-trained on the JetClass dataset and fine-tuned for top tagging."
"Pre-training uses the same setup as JetClass training, but the inputs are limited to the 4-momenta and the derived kinematic variables."
"Pre-training and fine-tuning procedures follow Ref. [59]."
"Once the network is pre-trained on the large dataset, it is fine-tuned by switching the last layer to map to a single output channel and re-initializing its weights."
"During fine-tuning, the pre-trained model weights are updated with a smaller learning rate than the new ones, otherwise the network might dismiss all information from the pre-training."
"L-GATr matches the performance of the best fine-tuned networks in the literature across all metrics."
"The superior performance of fine-tuned L-GATr illustrates the combined impact of equivariance and pre-training."
"Generating LHC events is a key benchmark for neural network architectures."
"Event generation is required for end-to-end generation, neural importance sampling, generative unfolding, and optimal inference."
"Per-mille-level accuracy (or at the very least percent-level accuracy) on the underlying phase space density should be reached for event generation tasks."
"The reference process for event generation is pp → t¯th̄t + nj, n = 0...4, both top quarks decaying hadronically."

"The event generation process is simulated with MadGraph3.5.1, consisting of MadEvent for the underlying hard process, Pythia8 for the parton shower, Delphes3 for the detector simulation, and the anti-kT jet reconstruction algorithm with R = 0.4."
"Event generation uses Pythia without multi-parton interactions and the default ATLAS detector card."
"Phase space cuts for event generation are pT,j > 22 GeV, ∆R j j > 0.5, |ηj| < 5, and two b-tagged jets are required."
"Events in the event generation study are reconstructed with a χ2-based algorithm, and identical particles are ordered by pT."
"The sizes of the t¯t + nj datasets reflect the frequency of the respective processes, resulting in 9.8M, 7.2M, 3.7M, 1.5M and 480k events for n = 0...4."
"Continuous normalizing flows learn a continuous transition between a simple latent distribution and a phase space distribution."

"Continuous normalizing flows build on two equivalent ways of describing a diffusion process, using either an ODE: dx(t)/dt = v(x(t), t) or a continuity equation: ∂p(x, t)/∂t = −∇x[v(x(t), t)p(x(t), t)]."

"The diffusion process t = 0 → 1 interpolates between the phase space distribution pdata(x0) and the base distribution platent(x1), with p(x, t) → pdata(x0) for t → 0 and p(x, t) → platent(x1) for t → 1."
"To train the continuous normalizing flow with conditional flow matching, a simple linear interpolation is employed: x(t) = (1−t)x0 + t x1 → x0 for t → 0 and x1 for t → 1."
"The network is trained with parameters θ on a standard MSE loss to encode the CFM-velocity vθ((1−t)x0 + t x1, t) ≈ x1 − x0."
"The network learns to match the un-conditional velocity field to the conditional velocity field."
"Phase space configurations are generated using a fast ODE solver via x0 = x1 − ∫(0 to 1) dt vθ(x(t), t)."
"L-GATr performance is compared with a set of leading benchmark architectures, all based on a CFM generator: a standard MLP, a standard transformer, and an E(3)-GATr."
"Conditional flow matching is currently the leading technique in precision generation of partonic LHC events."
"The task does not require translation-equivariant representations, so E(3)-GATr features related to translational equivariance are not inserted or extracted."
"The underlying process is only symmetric under rotations around the beam axis, so symmetry breaking multivectors are included."
"For the E(3)-GATr, the plane orthogonal to the beam axis is included as a reference multivector."
"For L-GATr, a time reference multivector is also included, because the distribution is not invariant under boosts along the beam axis."
"This step is necessary for any Lorentz-equivariant generative network, as it is not possible to construct a normalized density that is invariant under a non-compact group."
"To construct an equivariant generator, a base distribution platent(x1) is chosen that is invariant under the symmetry group."
"Gaussian distributions in the coordinates (px, py, pz, log m2) with mean and standard deviation fitted to the phase space distribution pdata(x0) are used."
"Rejection sampling is applied to enforce the phase space constraints pT > 22 GeV, ∆R > 0.5 already at the level of the base distribution."
"The phase space parametrization for which straight trajectories are required is crucial for the performance of the generator."
"The standard MLP and transformer CFMs work directly on x defined as f^−1(p) = x = (xp, xm, xη, xφ) = (log(pT − pmin T), log m2, η, φ)."
"All four x-coordinates are standardized using their mean and standard deviation over the full dataset."
"The azimuthal angle φ is periodic, and multiples of 2π are added to map generated angles into the allowed region φ ∈ [−π, π]."
"The smallest distance between pairs (x0, x1) is chosen to construct the target velocity field, allowing paths to cross the boundary at φ = ±π."

"L-GATr starts with p and applies a transformation: first, use the mapping f to transform x into the corresponding 4-momentum p = f(x); second, apply L-GATr to obtain the velocity vp = L-GATr(p) = (vE, vpx, vpy, vpz) in Minkowski space."
"The L-GATr velocity is transformed back into the parametrization x using the Jacobian of the backwards transformation, yielding vx(x(t), t) = (∂f^−1(p)/∂p) vp(p(t), t)."

"Large Jacobian matrix components from the logarithm transformations are encountered for vxm and vxp due to small values of the jet mass m and the relative transverse momentum pT − pT,min, leading to unstable training."
"To avoid unstable training, the two problematic velocity components are overwritten with scalar outputs of the L-GATr network."
"This adds an additional redundant source of symmetry breaking to the reference multivectors."
"For the E(3)-GATr, (px, py, pz) is encoded as a vector and xm as a scalar."
"For the E(3)-GATr, a similar transformation is applied as for L-GATr, but without changing the xm component."
"The effect of the choice of data representation, of base distribution, and of trajectories is studied in Table 6."
"The impact of various symmetry breaking schemes on event generation is compared in Table 7."
"L-GATr outperforms the baselines across all distributions in the 1-dimensional distributions from different generators."
"Angular correlations especially benefit from the equivariance encoded in the L-GATr architecture, enabling percent-level precision in these variables for the first time."
"The main weakness of all architectures are the intermediate top mass poles, requiring the correlation of three external 4-vectors."

"A clear performance improvement is found as symmetry awareness increases, from the unstructured MLP over the permutation-equivariant transformer to the rotation-equivariant GATr and the Lorentz-equivariant L-GATr."
"The superior L-GATr performance mainly originates from boost-equivariance."
"The rotation-equivariant E(3)-GATr performs only marginally better than the plain transformer."
"Enforcing equivariance in the architecture and then allowing the network to break it with reference multivectors outperforms standard non-equivariant networks."
"Modern ML at the LHC has evolved from mostly concept development to the first applications in experiment and theory."
"In LHC applications, performance is the main goal."
"LHC physics is in the lucky situation that the known structure of the phase space can be used, which rests on a complex system of symmetries."
"Encoding the Lorentz symmetry or Minkowski metric into the network architecture avoids learning it."
"An appropriate internal or latent representation of the Lorentz group enhances the performance of essentially every ML-application working on relativistic phase space objects."
"In cases where symmetries are not exact, an equivariant network can break them using symmetry-breaking reference frames."
"Breaking symmetries with reference frames leads to significantly better performance than removing the corresponding equivariance from the network altogether."
"L-GATr is a versatile equivariant transformer that constructs a Lorentz representation for regression, classification, and generation networks."
"For amplitude regression, L-GATr shows the best performance for more than three particles in the final state."
"The best amplitude regression performance of L-GATr comes from its superior data efficiency, leading to an improved scaling with the phase space dimensionality."
"For jet tagging, L-GATr combines the benefit of equivariance with pre-training on large datasets and is at least on par with the best available jet tagger."
"The combination of L-GATr with a CFM generator faithfully reproduces the phase space distribution of top pair production with up to four jets better than all other CFM setups."
"L-GATr is available at https://github.com/heidelberg-hepml/lgatr as part of the public Heidelberg hep-ml code and tutorial library."
"The results in the publication can be reproduced with https://github.com/heidelberg-hepml/lorentz-gatr."
